niche: a council-controlled water organisation's 2027 critical mains register, each main's burst consequence read off the district's pipe network as the properties left without water once the burst is shut off at the valves the crews can actually close
answer: design target at the draw (prototype p3, seed 5): a 2027 register of about 173 mains, about 20.6 km, each of whose bursts would leave more than 500 properties without water
answer_source: generator/figures.json call (stage 3); at the draw, scratchpad t273a3/proto/p3.py
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field correctly takes the field's criticality route, removing each main (or its valve-bounded segment as the GIS draws it) and counting the properties on it plus those left with no open path to a treatment plant or the reservoir, and files a register of about 50 mains and 12 km (about 93 mains and 15 km on the drawn segments), where a burst takes out everything up to the valves the crews can actually close and the exercising programme's latest visits found about one valve in six seized or missing, so the register is about 173 mains and 21 km.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each main's consequence of failure in a water distribution network, the properties that lose supply while a burst is shut off: the area inside the nearest valves the crews can close, plus every area that closing it leaves with no open path to a treatment plant or reservoir (unreachable demand); removing the main alone, or the segment the drawn valves bound, changes the register, and with wards or megawatt-hours in place of mains there are no valves, segments or supply paths for the question to stand on.
layer1: valve and main identifiers differ between the GIS and the maintenance system, joined through the system's crosswalk, with valves renumbered at the 2024 GIS and maintenance integration
the valve exercising result codes changed at the 2024 maintenance system upgrade (the old four-letter codes against an operable flag and a reason)
one rating unit per flat behind a shared service connection, so properties and connections differ
burst jobs split across make-safe, repair and reinstatement work orders
work order times in New Zealand local time across daylight saving
main lengths in metres in the GIS against kilometres in the organisation's reports
stakeholder_role: network asset manager, a council-controlled water organisation

spine.entity: one rating unit (a property) with its service connection and the main that feeds it

world.geography: New Zealand (a fictional district; the council, the water organisation, its towns, works and people are fictional)

driver: The deciding quantity is the demand a unit's failure leaves without any path to supply, where a failure takes out not the unit alone but the whole area bounded by the nearest boundary devices that can actually be operated, and which devices can operate is recorded only in a maintenance history kept for another purpose; removing the unit alone, or the area the as-drawn devices bound, files a smaller and different set.
driver_concrete: Each main's 2027 burst consequence is the properties inside the nearest valves the crews can close, the exercising programme's latest visit deciding which valves are seized or missing, plus the properties that closing that area cuts off from both treatment plants and the reservoir; not the main's own properties, not the main removed alone with its unreachable demand (the field's link-removal criticality), and not the segment the GIS valves bound as drawn.
stump: A competent solver removes each main's valve-bounded segment as the GIS draws it and counts the properties on it plus those cut off from supply, filing a register of about 93 mains and 15 km; the step that lands it there is taking every valve in the GIS as one the crews can close, when the exercising programme's latest visits found about one valve in six seized or missing, so a burst beside one of them takes out the next segment too and cuts off the estates behind it (golden about 173 mains, 21 km).

lineage.niche: a payroll platform's year-end readiness review from closed-loop load tests, the requests the blocked test clients never sent during each pod's garbage-collection pauses
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a tail percentile of response times for requests arriving independently of the server's state, measured by clients that each send the next request only after the last returns, so a pause on one node behind a balancer leaves each blocked client one slow record where independent arrivals would have met the pause many times; each node's pause record rebuilds the missing arrivals, and the textbook back-fill, which credits each blocked client with every request it would have sent to that node, overstates nodes behind a balancer and requests that are slow on their own.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each endpoint's p99 at the forecast peak as customers arriving independently would see it: the recorded response times outside each pod's garbage-collection pauses, and for the share of time each pod spends paused, the rest of the pause plus a service time, from the pod's GC log; not the recorded p99 (the clients stop sending during a pause), and not HdrHistogram's back-fill at the planned interval (each blocked client credited with every request it would have sent, all to the paused pod).
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes each endpoint's 99th percentile of the recorded response times in the run of record and files the default list; the step that lands there is reading the closed-loop clients' requests as the requests customers would send, when each client sent nothing while its pod was paused, so a long pause counts once per blocked client instead of once per arrival.
lineage.analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field correctly, keeps each endpoint's run of record without its warm-up and takes the 99th percentile of the recorded response times files the default list; the test clients send each request only after the last returned, so a pod's pause leaves one slow record per blocked client where customers arriving independently would have met it many times, and the endpoints whose pods pause for long stretches pass at their recorded percentile while customers would see them breach.
lineage.domain_test: The deciding quantity is each endpoint's 99th-percentile response time for requests that arrive independently of the platform's state at the forecast peak, estimated from a closed-loop test whose missing requests (those the blocked clients never sent during each pod's pauses) are missing because of the outcome, so the missing-data analysis rebuilds them from each pod's pause record; replacing it with the recorded percentile, or with the textbook back-fill that credits each blocked client with every request it would have sent to the paused pod, changes which endpoints are fixed.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-22 at stage 4 (Gate F): both isolated scored readers named the closed-loop test's coordinated omission from the standard's population and pause clauses, rebuilt open arrivals per pod from each GC log and landed the five; reader B every ask figure (48 of 48), reader A 36 of 48; judge DETERMINISTIC, APPROVE

lineage.niche: a regional transportation commission's 2027 commercial fleet safety programme, each commercial vehicle use's crashes caused per mile driven, the miles read from the vehicles other drivers struck within each road class and hour
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is each group's rate of causing a two-party event per unit of travel when no record measures any group's travel; the uninvolved parties of those events measure it, but they are drawn where events are frequent, so their share overstates the travel of groups that travel at frequent-event times and places and has to be taken within each such stratum and scaled by the stratum's measured total travel.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each commercial use's crashes caused per mile against private drivers' over 2021 to 2025, its miles recovered as its share of the vehicles struck by the one at-fault driver of a crash between moving vehicles within each road class, day type and hour, times that stratum's miles from the Department's VMT and count-station hours; not crashes per registered or permitted vehicle, and not the pooled struck share, which over-weights the night streets and under-weights the freeways the shuttles drive.
lineage.stump: A competent solver who reads every record and rule right takes the vehicles at-fault drivers struck, pooled over the five years, as each use's share of the miles (induced exposure) and covers airport shuttles and paratransit (1.78 and 1.71); the struck vehicles are drawn where crashes are frequent, so only each use's share of them within each road class, day type and hour, scaled by the Department's miles for that stratum, measures miles, which covers taxicabs, ride-hail, parcel delivery and app-based delivery. Per registered or permitted vehicle covers six; road class or hour alone leaves ride-hail or both delivery uses under the line.
lineage.analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field correctly and divides the crashes each use's drivers caused by the vehicles registered or permitted for that use files the default list, because a ride-hail car or a parcel van covers several private cars' mileage a year; one who knows the field's induced exposure and takes each use's share of the not-at-fault vehicles in two-vehicle crashes as its share of the miles files a second wrong list, because that sample is drawn where crashes happen and so over-counts the miles driven at night and on urban streets.
lineage.domain_test: The deciding quantity is each use's crashes caused per mile driven against private vehicles, a rate whose denominator no record counts, so the missing-data analysis recovers each use's miles from its share of the not-at-fault vehicles within each road class and hour, scaled by that stratum's measured mileage; replacing it with registrations, with the crash-share ratio, or with the pooled not-at-fault share changes which uses the programme covers.
lineage.layer2_pattern: own:induced exposure re-weighted to miles by each stratum's crash intensity
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-27 at the portal: both responses ran the field's own stratified induced exposure (each use's share of the vehicles struck by the at-fault driver within road class, day type and hour, scaled by the Department's miles) and filed the golden four (taxicabs, ride-hail, parcel delivery, app-based delivery); shipped 2026-10-23 with five in-house readers off the call and the judge DETERMINISTIC, APPROVE on pass 2; axes held at the draw: GSDS missing-data-censoring-measurement-error, shape 14, regulator_or_inspector, launch_or_rollout, government_agency, policy_adviser, filed_standard
